purpose: English-only public development candidates extending experimental explanation, school exclusion, vocational graph literacy and inclusive classroom experience. Identity, acquisition, full reading and writing value remain separate checks.

sources.title: London Education and Inclusion Project (LEIP): Exploring Negative and Null Effects of a Cluster-Randomised School-Intervention to Reduce School Exclusion—Findings from Protocol-Based Subgroup Analyses
sources.selection_question: How are prespecified subgroup expectations and unexpected intervention results used to advance an educational explanation without treating untested reasons as demonstrated mechanisms?
sources.version_note: Publisher open-access PDF. Subgroup report from an existing trial: do not count its main report as an independent intervention if later read. Confirm license and evidence before analysis.

sources.title: Does increasing social presence enhance the effectiveness of writing explanations?
sources.selection_question: How does a theory-driven experimental comparison distinguish an intended manipulation, experienced social presence and learning outcomes when the predicted pattern is not obtained?
sources.version_note: Publisher open-access PDF. Verify authors, design, primary outcomes, figures and access to any preregistration separately.

sources.title: Debunking misleading graphs effectively: How vocationally educated young adults perceive graphs
sources.selection_question: Do think-aloud accounts and the quantitative design comparison jointly explain graph interpretation, and what does the integration add beyond two parallel results sections?
sources.version_note: Publisher open-access English article. Actual integration and classification must be checked in the full text; a mixed-methods label is not sufficient.

sources.title: How do autistic students experience need-supportive teaching in mainstream secondary schools? A joint display analysis
sources.selection_question: How do matched classroom observations, student questionnaires and video-stimulated accounts change the interpretation of need-supportive teaching? Check whether student perspectives alter the meaning of observed utterances.
sources.version_note: Publisher labels this English article open access. License, authors and accessible full text require verification; abstract information is not completed reading.

sources.title: Developing empathy and support for students with the ‘most challenging behaviors:’ Mixed-methods outcomes of professional development in trauma-informed teaching practices
sources.selection_question: How are changed teacher reports and qualitative accounts integrated to explain professional learning while distinguishing perceptions, classroom practice and student outcomes?
sources.version_note: Publisher English full text. Confirm the study's integration and license; selection is a writing question, not an endorsement of its causal claims.
